title: Workshop synthesis & scale playbook — Brightline commerce POC
content:
Executive summary:

- Short version: Brightline's 3-week POC validated inference quality for customer-support summarization and measured the end-to-end latency/throughput envelope for expected shopping surge windows. Recommendation: two-phase rollout — (A) provision Dedicated capacity (EU + US) with an integrated KV caching tier for peak windows, then (B) evaluate a hybrid hosted/dedicated routing after 60 days of telemetry.

POC scope & what we executed:
- Feature: real-time customer chat summarization + contextual follow-ups (auto-suggest canned responses).
- Typical session profile: 3–6 messages, prompt ~120 tokens, response ~220 tokens.
- Models exercised: open-llm-16b-quant (cost-optimized), rdx-chat-7b-v1 (quality leader for follow-ups), rdx-11b-medium (fallback during complex contexts).
- Integration pattern: Brightline Node service -> Redwood API (temporary API key) -> responses stored to S3 for audit and eval sampling.
- Traffic: 10k sessions over 14 days (production-sampled + synthetic surge tests).

Primary results (observed during POC):
- Latency: p50=85ms, p90=210ms on Dedicated pool (aggregated 8k tokens/min).
- Cost signals: rdx-chat-7b ≈ $0.012 / 1k tokens; open-llm-16b-quant ≈ $0.006 / 1k tokens.
- Quality (human eval, n=300): rdx-chat-7b 87% acceptable, open-llm-16b-quant 78% acceptable (failure mode: hallucinated product IDs).
- Failure modes: transient request timeouts when concurrent sessions exceeded ~1.2x expected peak; coherence drops above ~1.2k token contexts.
- Efficiency note: KV cache produced ~18% higher effective throughput for repeat-context flows.

Technical takeaways:
- Prompt hygiene: adding a short system prompt + 3 few-shot examples reduced hallucinations by ~12%. We recommend Brightline lock canonical examples in a repo to control drift.
- Auth: currently using a shared API key — recommend per-service short-lived tokens with KMS-backed rotation.
- Data residency: EU customer data at rest requirement -> EU Dedicated or Private deployment for those tenants.
- SDK/integration: Node SDK worked but streaming disconnects need idempotent request IDs + clearer retry semantics.
- Observability: Brightline requested token-level cost by route and a per-customer SLA dashboard (we can expose via Console deliverable).

Deployment options (concise pros/cons + ballpark economics):
1) Dedicated (recommended initial):
   - Pros: predictable p95 latency, isolation for PII, straightforward SLA configuration.
   - Cons: baseline commit cost; EU Dedicated provisioning lead time ~2–3 weeks.
   - Ballpark: $18k/month reserved (covers ~1.2x current peak).
2) Hosted + smart routing (opportunistic overflow):
   - Pros: low marginal costs, good for burst overflow, minimal Brightline ops.
   - Cons: tail latency variability; limited data residency controls.
   - Ballpark: $0.008–$0.012 per 1k tokens (model-dependent, with discounts for commit).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Pros: full control, satisfies strict compliance/residency.
   - Cons: heavy Brightline ops integration, upfront onboarding.
   - Ballpark: setup $125k–$200k one-time + ~$40k/year license/support.

Immediate recommended actions (owners + ETA):
- Approve Dedicated baseline commit (owner: Maya Chen) — target decision by 2025-11-24. Deliverable: signed order for EU & US capacity.
- KMS & token plan (owner: Arjun Patel) — complete draft design by 2025-11-30. Deliverable: KMS policy + rotation schedule.
- Reliability hardening (owner: Riley Park) — implement idempotent request IDs & streaming retry policy by 2025-12-10.
- Telemetry & evals (owner: Sofia Alvarez) — deliver 12-week telemetry deck by 2025-12-05 (latency buckets, cost per route, quality regression triggers).
- Prompt canonization (owner: Leah Park at Brightline) — finalize canonical 50 prompts by 2025-11-14 (workshop captured 32).

Short risk register & mitigations:
- Model quality drift on quant variants: mitigation = automated evals on production-sampled prompts + canary traffic split + automatic rollback hooks.
- EU data residency provisioning delay: mitigation = temporary EU-to-US routing with data-at-rest controls until EU Dedicated node is ready.
- Spike throttling leading to timeouts: mitigation = token-bucket rate limiter + graceful degrade path that returns condensed summaries and a fallback short message.

Workshop notes / unanswered questions (for follow-up):
- Exact compliance checklist Brightline requires for EU PII workloads (DPA clauses, logging retention limits).
- SLA measurement window preferences (rolling 30-day vs calendar month).
- Preferred cadence for quality review and eval thresholds (suggest weekly for first 8 weeks).
- Brightline ops headcount to support Private deployment if chosen (estimate 1.0–1.5 FTE for initial onboarding).
